IPL 2026 – Exploratory Data Analysis¶

Match Analysis¶

Objective¶

Explore the integrated IPL 2026 dataset to understand its structure, identify important patterns, and prepare for further analysis.

Key activities¶

  • Load and inspect the integrated dataset.
  • Review data types and missing values.
  • Analyze match and innings-level information.
  • Explore scoring patterns and team performance.
  • Identify useful insights for the Power BI dashboard.
In [1]:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from pathlib import Path

# Project paths
PROJECT_DIR = Path.cwd().parent
CLEANED_DATA = PROJECT_DIR / "Cleaned-Data"

# Load integrated dataset
df = pd.read_csv(CLEANED_DATA / "ipl_2026_integrated.csv")

print("Dataset loaded successfully!")
print("Shape:", df.shape)

Step 2: Data Types and Missing Value Analysis¶

In this step, we will:

  • Inspect the data types of all columns.
  • Identify missing values and their percentages.
  • Distinguish between expected missing values and potential data-quality issues.

Step 3: Visualizing Missing Values¶

We will create a bar chart showing the percentage of missing values in each column.

This visualization helps identify columns with substantial missing data and supports decisions about which fields to use in subsequent analysis.

In [5]:
# Calculate missing percentages
missing_percent = (
    df.isnull().mean() * 100
).sort_values(ascending=False)

# Keep only columns with missing values
missing_percent = missing_percent[missing_percent > 0]

# Plot missing values
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

sns.barplot(
    x=missing_percent.values,
    y=missing_percent.index
)

plt.title("Missing Values by Column (%)")
plt.xlabel("Missing Values (%)")
plt.ylabel("Columns")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Step 5: Innings-Level Scoring Analysis¶

We will aggregate delivery-level records to calculate innings-level statistics.

Metrics:

  • Total runs scored
  • Runs scored from the bat
  • Extras conceded
  • Number of delivery records

These metrics will help us understand scoring patterns across matches and teams.

In [8]:
# Calculate innings-level statistics
innings_summary = (
    df.groupby(
        ["match_no", "date_delivery", "innings", "batting_team"],
        as_index=False
    )
    .agg(
        total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        total_extras=("extras", "sum"),
        delivery_records=("match_no", "size")
    )
)

# Calculate total innings score
innings_summary["innings_score"] = (
    innings_summary["total_runs"] +
    innings_summary["total_extras"]
)

display(innings_summary.head(10))

Step 6: Validating Innings Scores¶

We will compare calculated innings scores with the first- and second-innings scores recorded in the match metadata.

This check will help identify discrepancies between the delivery-level data and match-level statistics.

In [9]:
# Keep one row per match from the match metadata
match_scores = (
    df.dropna(subset=["match_id"])
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["match_id"])
    [[
        "match_id",
        "first_ings_score",
        "second_ings_score"
    ]]
    .copy()
)

# Prepare calculated innings scores for comparison
innings_wide = (
    innings_summary.pivot(
        index="match_no",
        columns="innings",
        values="innings_score"
    )
    .rename(columns={
        1: "calculated_first_innings",
        2: "calculated_second_innings"
    })
    .reset_index()
)

# Merge calculated scores with match metadata
score_comparison = innings_wide.merge(
    match_scores,
    left_on="match_no",
    right_on="match_id",
    how="inner"
)

# Calculate score differences
score_comparison["first_score_difference"] = (
    score_comparison["calculated_first_innings"]
    - score_comparison["first_ings_score"]
)

score_comparison["second_score_difference"] = (
    score_comparison["calculated_second_innings"]
    - score_comparison["second_ings_score"]
)

Step 7: Identifying All Score Discrepancies¶

We will identify matches where the calculated innings scores differ from the scores recorded in the match metadata.

We will count matching scores and mismatches separately for the first and second innings.

In [10]:
# Keep only rows where both scores are available
first_valid = score_comparison.dropna(
    subset=["calculated_first_innings", "first_ings_score"]
).copy()

second_valid = score_comparison.dropna(
    subset=["calculated_second_innings", "second_ings_score"]
).copy()

# Count matches and mismatches
print("First innings:")
print("Compared:", len(first_valid))
print("Matching:", (first_valid["first_score_difference"] == 0).sum())
print("Mismatches:", (first_valid["first_score_difference"] != 0).sum())

print("\nSecond innings:")
print("Compared:", len(second_valid))
print("Matching:", (second_valid["second_score_difference"] == 0).sum())
print("Mismatches:", (second_valid["second_score_difference"] != 0).sum())

# Display all mismatches
first_mismatches = first_valid[
    first_valid["first_score_difference"] != 0
][[
    "match_no",
    "calculated_first_innings",
    "first_ings_score",
    "first_score_difference"
]]

second_mismatches = second_valid[
    second_valid["second_score_difference"] != 0
][[
    "match_no",
    "calculated_second_innings",
    "second_ings_score",
    "second_score_difference"
]]

print("\nFirst innings mismatches:")
display(first_mismatches)

print("\nSecond innings mismatches:")
display(second_mismatches)

Step 8: Investigating Score Discrepancies¶

We will inspect the delivery records for Match 1, first innings.

The objective is to break down runs from the bat and extras, then compare the calculated total with the match metadata.

In [12]:
# Filter Match 1, first innings
match1_innings1 = df[
    (df["match_no"] == 1) &
    (df["innings"] == 1)
].copy()

# Summarize score components
print("Match 1 - First Innings")
print("Delivery records:", len(match1_innings1))
print("Runs from bat:", match1_innings1["runs_of_bat"].sum())
print("Total extras:", match1_innings1["extras"].sum())

print("\nExtras breakdown:")
display(
    match1_innings1[
        ["wide", "legbyes", "byes", "noballs"]
    ].sum().to_frame("Total")
)

# Calculated score
calculated_score = (
    match1_innings1["runs_of_bat"].sum()
    + match1_innings1["extras"].sum()
)

# Retrieve metadata score from the integrated dataset
metadata_score = (
    match1_innings1["first_ings_score"].dropna().iloc[0]
)

print("\nCalculated score:", calculated_score)
print("Metadata score:", metadata_score)
print("Difference:", calculated_score - metadata_score)

Inspect the complete over-by-over totals¶

In [15]:
over_summary = (
    match1_innings1
    .groupby("over", as_index=False)
    .agg(
        runs_from_bat=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        extras=("extras", "sum"),
        deliveries=("over", "size")
    )
)

over_summary["over_total"] = (
    over_summary["runs_from_bat"] + over_summary["extras"]
)
over_summary["cumulative_score"] = over_summary["over_total"].cumsum()

display(over_summary)

Finding — Match 1, first-innings score discrepancy¶

The delivery-level data produces a total of 203 runs (196 runs from the bat and 7 extras), whereas the match metadata reports 201. Inspection of the final deliveries confirms that the final delivery adds 2 runs, taking the calculated score from 201 to 203. The available data does not establish the cause of the discrepancy. The original records have been retained without correction.

7. Overall Match Analysis¶

In this section, we analyze the matches represented in the delivery-level dataset.

We will:

  • Count the unique matches in the delivery data.
  • Identify matches with and without match-level metadata.

Finding: Unusual Innings in Matches 12 and 38¶

  • Match 12 contains only one innings in the delivery data. Its match metadata identifies the match as abandoned.
  • Match 38 contains four innings in the delivery data. Match metadata confirms that it was a Super Over match.
  • The first two innings of Match 38 show scores of 154 and 155 in the delivery data, while metadata reports 155 for both innings.
  • The additional innings show LSG scoring 1 run and KKR scoring 4 runs in the delivery data.

These findings demonstrate why unusual innings counts and differences between delivery-level and match-level data should be investigated before calculating match statistics.

Calculate regulation-innings totals separately¶

In [26]:
# Calculate scores for the first two innings only
regulation_scores = (
    df[df["innings"].isin([1, 2])]
    .groupby(["match_no", "innings"], as_index=False)
    .agg(
        runs_from_bat=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        extras=("extras", "sum")
    )
)

regulation_scores["innings_score"] = (
    regulation_scores["runs_from_bat"] +
    regulation_scores["extras"]
)

# Put innings 1 and 2 into separate columns
regulation_match_scores = (
    regulation_scores
    .pivot(
        index="match_no",
        columns="innings",
        values="innings_score"
    )
    .rename(columns={
        1: "first_innings_score",
        2: "second_innings_score"
    })
    .reset_index()
)

regulation_match_scores["combined_regulation_runs"] = (
    regulation_match_scores["first_innings_score"] +
    regulation_match_scores["second_innings_score"]
)

Finding: Incomplete and Low-Scoring Matches¶

  • Match 12 has only one recorded innings, with 25 runs. Its match metadata identifies it as abandoned.
  • Match 39 has the lowest combined regulation score in the current dataset, with 152 runs (75 and 77).
  • Match 3, Match 5, and Match 51 are also among the five lowest first-innings scores.

Incomplete matches should be handled separately when calculating statistics for completed matches.

Key Findings: Match Score Analysis¶

The analysis of 73 matches with both innings recorded revealed the following:

  • The average first-innings score was 194.88 runs, compared with 180 runs in the second innings.
  • The median first-innings score was 199, while the second-innings median was 182.
  • Both innings had nearly identical standard deviations (36.49 and 36.57).
  • The middle 50% of first-innings scores ranged from 163 to 222, compared with 160 to 205 for second innings.
  • Both innings had a maximum recorded score of 264.
  • Match 12 was excluded from the comparison because it was abandoned and had no recorded second innings.

These findings describe the score patterns in the available dataset. They do not establish the causes of the differences between innings.

Calculate team wins from available metadata¶

]

8.4 Team Win Percentage¶

Calculate each team's win percentage using only matches with available metadata and a recorded winner.

Win Percentage = (Wins / Matches with recorded results) × 100

In [36]:
# Get the teams participating in matches with recorded results
team_appearances = pd.concat([
    completed_results[["match_id", "match_winner"]]
    .rename(columns={"match_winner": "team"}),

    completed_results[["match_id", "match_winner"]]
    .merge(
        df[["match_id", "batting_team", "bowling_team"]]
        .drop_duplicates(subset=["match_id"]),
        on="match_id",
        how="left"
    )[["match_id", "batting_team", "bowling_team"]]
    .melt(
        id_vars="match_id",
        value_vars=["batting_team", "bowling_team"],
        value_name="team"
    )[["match_id", "team"]]
]).drop_duplicates(subset=["match_id", "team"])

# Count appearances per team
team_match_counts = (
    team_appearances.groupby("team")["match_id"]
    .nunique()
    .reset_index(name="matches_with_results")
)

# Combine appearances and wins
team_performance = team_match_counts.merge(
    team_wins,
    on="team",
    how="left"
)

team_performance["wins"] = team_performance["wins"].fillna(0).astype(int)

team_performance["win_percentage"] = (
    team_performance["wins"] /
    team_performance["matches_with_results"] * 100
).round(2)

team_performance = team_performance.sort_values(
    "win_percentage", ascending=False
).reset_index(drop=True)

display(team_performance)

Team Performance — Key Findings¶

  • The dataset contains 10 teams participating in the available delivery records.
  • PBKS has a recorded win percentage of 100% across 6 matches with known results.
  • RCB has 6 wins from 8 matches, followed by SRH with 5 wins from 8 matches.
  • GT and RR have identical recorded win percentages of 50%.
  • CSK, DC, and LSG each have a recorded win percentage of 37.5%.
  • KKR and MI have the lowest recorded win percentages at 28.57%.
  • These results are based on the available match metadata, not complete season standings. Team comparisons should be interpreted with this limitation in mind.

9.6 Calculate Batting Strike Rate¶

Combine total runs, innings played, and balls faced to calculate the strike rate of each batter.

Strike Rate = (Total Runs / Balls Faced) × 100

In [50]:
# Combine batting metrics
batting_summary = (
    player_runs
    .merge(player_innings, on="striker", how="left")
    .merge(balls_faced, on="striker", how="left")
)

# Calculate strike rate
batting_summary["strike_rate"] = (
    batting_summary["total_runs"] /
    batting_summary["balls_faced"] * 100
).round(2)

# Display top 10 run scorers with their batting metrics
display(
    batting_summary
    .sort_values("total_runs", ascending=False)
    .head(10)
)

9.7 Boundary Analysis¶

Analyze the number of fours and sixes hit by each batter.

Calculate total boundaries and runs scored through boundaries to understand each batter's boundary contribution.

In [51]:
# Calculate fours and sixes for each batter
boundary_summary = (
    df.groupby("striker")
    .agg(
        fours=("runs_of_bat", lambda x: (x == 4).sum()),
        sixes=("runs_of_bat", lambda x: (x == 6).sum())
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Calculate total boundaries
boundary_summary["total_boundaries"] = (
    boundary_summary["fours"] + boundary_summary["sixes"]
)

# Calculate runs scored through boundaries
boundary_summary["boundary_runs"] = (
    boundary_summary["fours"] * 4 +
    boundary_summary["sixes"] * 6
)

# Display top 10 players by boundary runs
display(
    boundary_summary
    .sort_values("boundary_runs", ascending=False)
    .head(10)
)

9.8 Boundary Contribution Percentage¶

Calculate the percentage of each batter's total runs that came from fours and sixes.

Boundary Percentage = (Boundary Runs / Total Runs) × 100

In [52]:
# Combine boundary data with total runs
boundary_analysis = boundary_summary.merge(
    player_runs,
    on="striker",
    how="left"
)

# Calculate boundary contribution percentage
boundary_analysis["boundary_percentage"] = (
    boundary_analysis["boundary_runs"] /
    boundary_analysis["total_runs"] * 100
).round(2)

# Display top 10 run scorers and their boundary contribution
display(
    boundary_analysis
    .sort_values("total_runs", ascending=False)
    [[
        "striker",
        "total_runs",
        "fours",
        "sixes",
        "boundary_runs",
        "boundary_percentage"
    ]]
    .head(10)
)

10.4 Bowling figures: runs conceded and legal deliveries¶

A bowler is charged for batter runs and wides. Byes and leg-byes are not charged to the bowler. Legal balls exclude wides and no-balls. We will calculate a provisional version using the available columns and check whether no-ball data is present.

In [57]:
# Provisional bowling runs conceded
df["bowler_runs_conceded"] = (
    df["runs_of_bat"] + df["wide"]
)

# Legal deliveries, excluding wides
df["legal_ball"] = (df["wide"] == 0).astype(int)

# Aggregate bowling figures
bowling_summary = (
    df.groupby("bowler")
    .agg(
        runs_conceded=("bowler_runs_conceded", "sum"),
        legal_balls=("legal_ball", "sum"),
        wickets=("bowler", "size")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Replace the temporary wicket count with credited wickets
bowler_wickets = (
    df[df["wicket_type"].isin([
        "caught", "bowled", "lbw", "stumped",
        "hit wicket", "hitwicket"
    ])]
    .groupby("bowler")
    .size()
    .rename("wickets")
)

bowling_summary = bowling_summary.drop(columns="wickets").merge(
    bowler_wickets,
    on="bowler",
    how="left"
)

bowling_summary["wickets"] = (
    bowling_summary["wickets"].fillna(0).astype(int)
)

# Economy rate = runs conceded / overs (legal balls / 6)
bowling_summary["overs"] = bowling_summary["legal_balls"] / 6
bowling_summary["economy"] = (
    bowling_summary["runs_conceded"] / bowling_summary["overs"]
)

display(
    bowling_summary.sort_values(
        "wickets", ascending=False
    ).head(10).round(2)
)

This validation helps ensure that runs conceded, legal balls, and economy rates are calculated correctly.

10.6 — Correct the bowling figures¶

In [59]:
# Calculate runs conceded by the bowler
df["bowler_runs_conceded"] = (
    df["runs_of_bat"] + df["wide"] + df["noballs"]
)

# A delivery is legal only if it is neither a wide nor a no-ball
df["legal_ball"] = (
    (df["wide"] == 0) & (df["noballs"] == 0)
).astype(int)

# Aggregate runs and legal balls by bowler
bowling_summary = (
    df.groupby("bowler")
    .agg(
        runs_conceded=("bowler_runs_conceded", "sum"),
        legal_balls=("legal_ball", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Count bowler-credited wickets
bowler_wickets = (
    df[df["wicket_type"].isin([
        "caught", "bowled", "lbw", "stumped",
        "hit wicket", "hitwicket"
    ])]
    .groupby("bowler")
    .size()
    .rename("wickets")
)

bowling_summary = bowling_summary.merge(
    bowler_wickets,
    on="bowler",
    how="left"
)

bowling_summary["wickets"] = (
    bowling_summary["wickets"].fillna(0).astype(int)
)

# Economy rate
bowling_summary["economy"] = (
    bowling_summary["runs_conceded"] * 6
    / bowling_summary["legal_balls"]
)

# Display top 10 wicket-takers
display(
    bowling_summary.sort_values(
        "wickets", ascending=False
    ).head(10).round(2)
)

Step 10.7: Bowling Average and Bowling Strike Rate¶

Bowling average and bowling strike rate help us understand how frequently a bowler takes wickets and how many runs they concede to take each wicket.

  • Bowling Average = Runs Conceded / Wickets
  • Bowling Strike Rate = Legal Balls / Wickets

These metrics complement economy rate and wicket totals when comparing bowling performances.

In [60]:
# Calculate bowling average
bowling_summary["bowling_average"] = (
    bowling_summary["runs_conceded"]
    / bowling_summary["wickets"].replace(0, np.nan)
)

# Calculate bowling strike rate
bowling_summary["bowling_strike_rate"] = (
    bowling_summary["legal_balls"]
    / bowling_summary["wickets"].replace(0, np.nan)
)

# View top 10 wicket-takers with additional metrics
display(
    bowling_summary.sort_values(
        "wickets", ascending=False
    )[
        [
            "bowler",
            "runs_conceded",
            "legal_balls",
            "wickets",
            "economy",
            "bowling_average",
            "bowling_strike_rate"
        ]
    ].head(10).round(2)
)

Step 10.8: Bowling Performance Analysis¶

The bowling summary provides useful insights into the performance of bowlers in the dataset.

  • Wickets: Kagiso Rabada leads the top 10 wicket-takers with 29 wickets, followed by Bhuvneshwar Kumar with 28.
  • Economy rate: Sunil Narine has the lowest economy rate among these bowlers at 6.60.
  • Bowling average: Bhuvneshwar Kumar has the lowest bowling average at 17.86.
  • Bowling strike rate: Kagiso Rabada has the lowest bowling strike rate at 13.38 balls per wicket.

These metrics highlight different aspects of bowling performance. Economy measures run control, bowling average measures runs conceded per wicket, and bowling strike rate measures how frequently a bowler takes wickets.

The observations are limited to the top 10 wicket-takers in the available dataset.

Step 10.10: Summary of Batting and Bowling Analysis¶

Batting Analysis¶

  • Top run-scorer: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi leads with 776 runs.
  • Highest strike rate among the top 10 run-scorers: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, with a strike rate of 237.31.
  • Boundary contribution: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 684 runs through fours and sixes, accounting for 88.14% of his total runs.

Bowling Analysis¶

  • Lowest bowling average: Bhuvneshwar Kumar recorded a bowling average of 17.86.

Overall Insights¶

The batting analysis highlights differences in run-scoring volume, strike rate, and boundary contribution. The bowling analysis compares wicket-taking frequency, run control, and bowling efficiency.

Together, these metrics provide a more detailed view of individual batting and bowling performances in the available IPL 2026 delivery dataset.

Step 11: Match-Level Analysis¶

Match-level analysis helps us understand scoring patterns across the tournament. We will aggregate delivery-level data to calculate total runs scored in each match and examine scoring trends.

11.1 Match-Level Run Aggregation¶

Calculate total runs for each match by summing batter runs and extras across all innings.

In [63]:
# Calculate total runs at match level
match_totals = (
    df.groupby("match_no")
    .agg(
        total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        total_extras=("extras", "sum"),
        innings_count=("innings", "nunique")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

match_totals["match_total"] = (
    match_totals["total_runs"] + match_totals["total_extras"]
)

display(match_totals.head(10))
print("Total matches:", match_totals["match_no"].nunique())

11.6.1 First vs. Second Innings Score Distribution¶

A box plot compares the score distributions of the first and second innings.

It helps us examine:

  • Median: The middle score for each innings.
  • Interquartile range (IQR): The spread of the middle 50% of scores.
  • Outliers: Scores that fall unusually far from the central distribution.

We will use the available innings data and distinguish the two innings with IPL-inspired blue and gold colors.

In [69]:
# Keep only the first two innings
regulation_innings = innings_summary[
    innings_summary["innings"].isin([1, 2])
].copy()

# Create innings labels
regulation_innings["innings_label"] = (
    regulation_innings["innings"]
    .map({1: "First Innings", 2: "Second Innings"})
)

# IPL-inspired colors
innings_palette = {
    "First Innings": "#1E3A8A",
    "Second Innings": "#D4A017"
}

plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))

sns.boxplot(
    data=regulation_innings,
    x="innings_label",
    y="innings_score",
    hue="innings_label",
    palette=innings_palette,
    legend=False
)

plt.title("First vs. Second Innings Score Distribution - IPL 2026")
plt.xlabel("Innings")
plt.ylabel("Runs Scored")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

11.7 Statistical Comparison of Innings Scores¶

Calculate descriptive statistics for first- and second-innings scores.

  • Mean: Average runs scored per innings.
  • Median: Middle score, less affected by extreme values.
  • Standard deviation: Measures how widely scores vary around the mean.

These statistics will help quantify the differences observed in the box plot.

In [70]:
# Calculate descriptive statistics by innings
innings_stats = (
    regulation_innings
    .groupby("innings_label")["innings_score"]
    .agg(
        matches="count",
        mean="mean",
        median="median",
        std="std",
        minimum="min",
        maximum="max"
    )
    .round(2)
)

# Display in the correct innings order
innings_stats = innings_stats.reindex([
    "First Innings",
    "Second Innings"
])

display(innings_stats)

12.2 Venue-Level Match and Scoring Analysis¶

Group the delivery data by match and venue to calculate match-level total runs. Then aggregate by venue to identify:

  • Number of matches played at each venue.
  • Average total runs per match.
  • Highest and lowest match totals at each venue.

Using match-level totals prevents venues with longer matches or more deliveries from being overcounted.

In [74]:
# Create match-level totals with venue information
venue_match_totals = (
    df.groupby(["match_no", "venue_delivery"])
    .agg(
        total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        total_extras=("extras", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

venue_match_totals["match_total"] = (
    venue_match_totals["total_runs"]
    + venue_match_totals["total_extras"]
)

# Aggregate scoring statistics by venue
venue_summary = (
    venue_match_totals
    .groupby("venue_delivery")
    .agg(
        matches=("match_no", "nunique"),
        avg_match_total=("match_total", "mean"),
        highest_total=("match_total", "max"),
        lowest_total=("match_total", "min")
    )
    .sort_values("matches", ascending=False)
    .round(2)
    .reset_index()
)

Venue Analysis — Key Findings¶

  • Sawai Mansingh Stadium, Jaipur recorded the highest average match total of 432 runs across 4 matches.
  • Barsapara Cricket Stadium, Guwahati had the lowest average match total of 310.67 runs across 3 matches.
  • Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai recorded an average of 419 runs across 7 matches, with a maximum match total of 488.

Toss Analysis — Key Findings¶

  • Teams chose to bowl first in 34 of 38 completed matches (89.47%).
  • Teams chose to bat first in only 4 completed matches (10.53%).
  • The toss-winning team also won 21 of 38 completed matches (55.26%).
  • Among teams choosing to bowl, the toss winner won 20 of 34 matches (58.82%).
  • Among teams choosing to bat, the toss winner won 1 of 4 matches (25%).

Conclusion: Bowling first was the dominant toss decision in the available completed matches. The toss-winning team won slightly more than half of the matches. However, the small sample—particularly for the bat-first decision—limits comparisons and does not establish a causal relationship between toss decisions and match outcomes.

Data limitation: The dataset contains 74 match IDs, but only 38 completed matches with usable match metadata for this analysis.

15.2 Classifying Deliveries into Match Phases¶

Group deliveries into three phases based on the over number:

  • Powerplay: overs 0–5 (overs 1–6)
  • Middle overs: overs 6–14 (overs 7–15)
  • Death overs: overs 15–19 (overs 16–20)

The integer part of the over.ball value identifies the over index.

In [86]:
# Extract the over index from the over.ball notation
df["over_number"] = np.floor(df["over"]).astype(int)

# Assign match phases
def assign_phase(over):
    if 0 <= over <= 5:
        return "Powerplay"
    elif 6 <= over <= 14:
        return "Middle Overs"
    elif 15 <= over <= 19:
        return "Death Overs"
    else:
        return "Beyond 20 Overs"

df["phase"] = df["over_number"].apply(assign_phase)

# Check the number of delivery records in each phase
phase_counts = (
    df["phase"]
    .value_counts()
    .reindex(["Powerplay", "Middle Overs", "Death Overs", "Beyond 20 Overs"])
    .fillna(0)
    .astype(int)
)

display(phase_counts.to_frame("delivery_records"))

15.3 Phase-wise Scoring and Wickets¶

Calculate total runs, legal deliveries, run rate, and recorded wickets for the powerplay, middle overs, and death overs.

Run rate is calculated as total runs divided by legal deliveries, multiplied by 6.

In [87]:
# Calculate total runs and identify legal deliveries
df["total_runs"] = df["runs_of_bat"] + df["extras"]

df["is_legal_delivery"] = (
    (df["wide"] == 0) & (df["noballs"] == 0)
)

# Summarize scoring by phase
phase_summary = (
    df[df["phase"].isin(["Powerplay", "Middle Overs", "Death Overs"])]
    .groupby("phase")
    .agg(
        total_runs=("total_runs", "sum"),
        legal_deliveries=("is_legal_delivery", "sum"),
        wickets=("wicket_type", lambda x: x.notna().sum())
    )
    .reindex(["Powerplay", "Middle Overs", "Death Overs"])
    .reset_index()
)

phase_summary["run_rate"] = (
    phase_summary["total_runs"] /
    phase_summary["legal_deliveries"] * 6
).round(2)

display(phase_summary)
phase total_runs legal_deliveries wickets run_rate

16. Final EDA Summary — IPL 2026¶

1. Dataset Overview¶

  • Analyzed IPL 2026 match and ball-by-ball delivery data.
  • The deliveries dataset contains 17,477 records.
  • The match metadata contains 39 matches, while the delivery dataset contains 74 distinct match IDs.

2. Match Scoring Analysis¶

  • First innings average score: 194.88 runs across 73 innings.
  • Second innings average score: 180 runs across 73 innings.
  • Highest combined match total: 528 runs.
  • The incomplete abandoned match was excluded from the complete-innings comparison.

3. Batting Analysis¶

  • Vaibhav Sooryavanshi led the available batting statistics with 776 runs.
  • Shubman Gill scored 732 runs.
  • Sai Sudharsan scored 722 runs.
  • Batting analysis included runs, balls faced, strike rates, and boundary contributions.

4. Bowling Analysis¶

  • Kagiso Rabada led the recorded wicket analysis with 29 wickets.
  • Bhuvneshwar Kumar recorded 28 wickets.
  • Jofra Archer recorded 25 wickets.
  • Bowling analysis included wickets, economy rate, bowling average, and bowling strike rate.

5. Venue Analysis¶

  • Sawai Mansingh Stadium, Jaipur had the highest average match total at 432 runs across 4 matches.
  • Barsapara Cricket Stadium, Guwahati had the lowest average at 310.67 runs across 3 matches.
  • Venue averages were interpreted with consideration for differing sample sizes.

6. Toss Analysis¶

  • Teams chose to bowl first in 34 of 38 completed matches.
  • The toss-winning team also won 21 of 38 completed matches (55.26%).
  • The toss-winning teams choosing to bowl won 20 of 34 matches (58.82%).
  • Only 4 teams chose to bat first, limiting comparisons between decisions.

7. Match Outcomes¶

  • RCB and PBKS recorded 6 wins each in the available completed-match metadata.
  • SRH recorded 5 wins.
  • The outcome analysis was limited to 38 completed matches with recorded winners.

8. Phase-wise Scoring¶

  • Middle overs contributed the most total runs: 12,012.
  • Death overs had the highest run rate: 10.76 runs per over.
  • Powerplay run rate was 10.08, while middle-overs run rate was 9.29.
  • The middle overs had the highest number of recorded wickets: 361.

9. Data Limitations¶

  • The delivery data contains 74 distinct match IDs, but the match metadata covers only 39.
  • Some match totals and results could not be reconciled between the two sources.
  • Abandoned and incomplete matches require special handling.
  • Venue, toss, and outcome findings based on metadata have limited coverage.
  • Some player statistics contain inconsistencies that were identified during the data audit.

10. Conclusion¶

The exploratory analysis examined match scoring, batting, bowling, venues, toss decisions, match outcomes, and scoring phases in the available IPL 2026 dataset.

The findings provide a foundation for building visual reports and interactive dashboards. Data coverage and validation limitations should be considered when interpreting the results.

Next phase: Develop focused visualizations and an interactive Power BI dashboard using the cleaned and validated data.
